primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Pendred syndrome due to SLC26A4 loss
mechanism: Pendrin, encoded by SLC26A4, functions as an apical anion exchanger in thyroid and inner-ear epithelia. In thyroid follicular cells, loss of pendrin reduces iodide efflux into the follicular lumen and impairs iodide organification; inner-ear dysfunction causes sensorineural hearing loss and enlarged vestibular aqueducts.
vignette: A 12-year-old girl has bilateral sensorineural hearing loss that began in early childhood. Temporal-bone imaging shows enlarged vestibular aqueducts. She now has a painless goiter. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC26A4.
lead: Which of the following transport abnormalities most directly explains the thyroid component of this disorder?
correct: Reduced apical efflux of iodide from thyroid follicular cells into the follicular lumen
distractors: Reduced basolateral uptake of iodide from blood through the sodium-iodide symporter
Failure of thyroid peroxidase to oxidize iodide and couple iodotyrosine residues
Failure of thyroglobulin synthesis in the rough endoplasmic reticulum
Constitutive activation of the TSH receptor Gs-cAMP signaling pathway
distractor_notes: The sodium-iodide symporter mediates basolateral iodide uptake into thyrocytes. Pendrin functions apically and participates in iodide movement toward the follicular lumen.
Thyroid peroxidase catalyzes oxidation and organification after iodide reaches the lumen; in Pendred syndrome the primary defect is upstream apical anion transport.
Thyroglobulin synthesis defects can impair hormone production but do not explain the SLC26A4-related combination of goiter and inner-ear disease.
Activating TSH receptor mutations cause autonomous hyperthyroidism, not sensorineural hearing loss with enlarged vestibular aqueducts.
key_expl: Pendred syndrome is caused by biallelic SLC26A4 variants. SLC26A4 encodes pendrin, an apical anion exchanger expressed in the thyroid and inner ear. In the thyroid, reduced pendrin function decreases iodide efflux into the follicular lumen and impairs organification, promoting goiter. In the inner ear, altered anion transport disrupts endolymphatic homeostasis and is associated with enlarged vestibular aqueducts and sensorineural hearing loss.
objective: Explain Pendred syndrome as loss of SLC26A4/pendrin-mediated apical anion transport, including reduced thyroid iodide efflux into the follicular lumen.
